item.title: HTB: Nanocorp - Active Directory Hard Walkthrough
item.description: NanoCorp is a Hard Windows Active Directory machine featuring a realistic exploit chain that combines recent Windows vulnerabilities with Active Directory misconfigurations. The attack begins by exploiting CVE-2025-24071 to trigger an NTLM hash leakage using a malicious ZIP archive. After successfully cracking the hash, Active Directory enumeration reveals several misconfigured ACL permissions, enabling privilege escalation to the monitoring_svc account. This account, being a member of the Protected Users group, requires Kerberos authentication to establish WinRM access. Finally, exploiting CVE-2024-0670 within the Checkmk agent grants full NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges on the Domain Controller.

item.title: Piryt with Gandlaf
item.description:
Gandalf is an educational platform that helps organizations understand AI security risks through hands-on experience. Players try to outsmart Lakera’s AI character by crafting strategic prompts to bypass its defenses. As the game progresses, Gandalf’s security measures adapt, teaching participants how AI vulnerabilities evolve—and how to defend against them. By playing Gandalf, teams learn firsthand how AI vulnerabilities work and why securing AI requires more than conventional defenses.

LLM Red Teaming Framework Setup (PyRIT)

To systematically test the Target LLM for prompt injection vulnerabilities, we integrate the Lakera AI Gandalf CTF API into Microsoft’s PyRIT framework. This implementation enables automated single-turn interactions, payload conversion (e.g., Base64, ROT13), and automated adversarial scoring.

item.title: Windows Internals: From x86_64 Assembly to Position-Independent Shellcode Mechanics
item.description:
Understanding payload execution at the binary level requires stripping away high-level abstractions and observing how the CPU processes raw machine code. Whether generating payloads via Metasploit (msfvenom) or compiling custom position-independent shellcode (PIC), the underlying compilation pipeline follows a deterministic path from assembly source code down to raw opcodes.

This write-up breaks down the internal mechanics of transforming x86_64 assembly into a clean, position-independent byte array, analyzing ELF object structures, relocation traps, and binary extraction workflows.
